toxicity.Notes: Acute oral toxicity following OECD TG 420, section 2.7.1: ten Sprague Dawley rats of 160-180 g, both sexes, randomised into five groups of two (one of each sex) - a control given 0.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose at 10 mL/kg and test groups at 20, 120, 200 and 2000 mg/kg by oral gavage - and kept under observation for three days. The result states that the LD50 dose of the complex was found at 120 mg/kg with no treatment-related mortality in the other treated groups; the abstract phrases the same number as the dose at which the complex showed mortality. No per-dose mortality counts are given, so survival_pct stays empty, and the group of two is the whole cohort. Group_size is the two animals per dose. The 28-day repeated oral study in twenty rats at 10, 20, 45 and 90 mg/kg found raised WBC, bilirubin, ALT, AST, ALP, creatinine and BUN, lowered total protein and histopathological damage to kidney, liver, stomach and testis at 90 mg/kg only; that is organ toxicity and belongs to the separate pass. The anticancer work is DMH plus DSS induced colon carcinogenesis in male Wistar rats scored by aberrant crypt foci counts and immunohistochemistry, with no tumour volume or weight, so there is no main row. The same group's vanadium-quercetin paper, 10.1007/s10534-018-0117-3, reports the same LD50 of 120 mg/kg for that complex in BALB/c mice. Treatment arm (column removed 2026-11-09): vanadium luteolin complex, single oral dose, OECD TG 420. Cohort (column removed 2026-11-09): cbf3322-ld50.
